title.narrative: Guidance to green the Kenyan healthcare sector

description.narrative: Climate change and health are intricately linked. At the COP26, where Kenya publicly committed to delivering both net zero (by 2030) and climate-resilient healthcare, the need for the health sector to adapt to climate change, as well as contribute to climate mitigation and to make health facilities greener was undersigned by many countries.The aim of this project is to support the Kenyan Ministry of Health in drafting Green Guidelines for the Health Sector that will lead the sector into more sustainable, green and climate mitigating practices, to reduced CO2 emissions, improved health outcomes, and long-term access and cost savings for healthcare institutions. Dutch lessons learned and experience regarding the greening of the health sector, as well as Dutch green innovations and private sector solutions, will be shared. This Government-to-Government cooperation between the Dutch Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport and the Kenyan Ministry of Health will on the one hand support Kenya's ambition to reduce CO2 emissions and to mitigate climate in the healthcare sector. On the other hand, Dutch innovations and solutions from the private sector will be promoted.This project is part of the Life Science and Health combi-track in Kenya, as well as the Global Health Partnership Programme of the Dutch Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport.
